definitions.hwAssignment: Homework is assigned at the end of most weeks and is generally due the following week, uploaded to Canvas (JPEG files only) and in some cases also brought to class. Assignments typically pair several short timed studies (2-5 minutes each) with one sustained large-format drawing representing roughly 5-6 hours of work. Students should expect to spend 4–6 hours per week outside of class on coursework.
definitions.sketchbook: A sketchbook must be maintained throughout the semester for exercises, experimentation, written reflections, and visual research. Just one sketchbook; recommended sizes 5x8 or 9x12.
definitions.portfolio: A portfolio of all assignments, exercises, and final projects must be maintained throughout the semester. You also need a physical portfolio large enough to carry and store large-format works.
definitions.attendance: Arriving more than 10 minutes late is considered tardy. Three tardies equal one absence. Students who reach three unexcused absences receive a failing grade for the course; at three absences, documentation from your dean is required to avoid failing. Attendance at the first class is required.
definitions.participation: Attendance and active participation are essential and central to success. Students are expected to arrive prepared with required materials, be on time, contribute to critiques and discussions, and complete all assignments on schedule. Growth and sustained effort over the semester are emphasized as much as technical skill. Worth 30% of the grade.
definitions.critique: Studio projects are reviewed in group critiques. For the midterm and final projects the class is split into two critique groups that present on consecutive class days — group 1 on Monday, group 2 on Wednesday. You must bring the finished work to class for your assigned critique group.
definitions.embodiedStudioPractice: The course may include brief, optional exercises such as stretching, breathing, movement, or collaborative activities during studio time. Participation is encouraged but not required, students may opt out or modify participation, and these activities are not evaluative.
definitions.studioCleaning: The final 10 minutes of each scheduled class are reserved for cleanup. Because the studio is shared, students clean up any mess they create both during class and during independent studio time. There is a door code for studio access outside class hours.
definitions.readingList: Readings supplement studio practice throughout the semester: The Labor of Looking (Anoka Faruqee); How Art Can Be Thought: A Handbook for Change (De Souza, excerpt pp. 7-9); Zen in the Art of Archery (Eugen Herrigel, selected readings); Drawing As Destination Forever Arriving (Mei Kazama).
definitions.materials: Keep material cost around $100 or less. Student-supplied: sketchbook, drawing board with clip, large drawing pad (Strathmore 400 Series or Canson, 18"x24", mixed media paper), kneaded eraser, pencils (2H, HB, 2B, 3B, 4B, 6B), sharpener, portfolio. Provided by class: newsprint 18x24, watercolor paper, color pencils, cardboard drawing paper, glue stick and collage material, some extra paper, charcoal (vine/compressed, various weights) and drawing materials in limited amounts, kneaded eraser, large drawing pad for class use.

gradingPolicy: Evaluation is based approximately on: 30% participation and preparedness; 45% studio projects and assignments; 25% final project. Grades are determined by the completion and quality of studio projects, homework assignments, attendance, midterm portfolio, and the final project, along with thoughtful engagement in critiques and discussions. Three unexcused absences result in a failing grade. Any extra credit or missing assignments must be submitted by December 18 at 11:59 PM — no exceptions after that deadline.

items.summary: Gather materials; three contour and three blind contour drawings in your sketchbook; read Zen in the Art of Archery ch. 1-2 and write a reflection. Canvas upload — JPEGs only.
items.verbatim: HW Assignment: Gather required materials. Complete three contour drawings (3–5 minutes each) and three blind contour drawings (2–3 minutes each) in your sketchbook with pencils. Read Chapters 1–2 of Zen in the Art of Archery and write a short reflection in your sketchbook responding to the reading (Canvas upload, due Sept 9… please only upload JPEG FILES!)

items.summary: Three quick cross-contour/value studies of a home still life plus one sustained large-format still life (3 objects, strong light source), ~5-6 hours. Canvas upload.
items.verbatim: HW Assignment: Complete three quick studies (2–5 minutes each) using cross-contour and value of a home still life, and one sustained still life drawing on your large format paper using pencils. The still life should include three objects with a strong light source. Spend approximately 5-6 hours on large drawing paper. Due Sept 16 (Canvas upload).

items.summary: Three drapery sketches plus one sustained large-format pencil drapery still life (~5-6 hours), and a sketchbook reflection on Zen ch. 3. Due in class and on Canvas.
items.verbatim: HW Assignment: Complete three drapery sketches (3–5 minutes each; to lock in a composition for sustained drawing) and one sustained pencil drapery still life drawing with a strong light source on large-format paper. Spend approximately 5–6 hours on the sustained drawing. Read Chapter 3 of Zen in the Art of Archery and write a short sketchbook reflection. Due Sept 23 (in-class and Canvas upload)
